name: LME49990 / LME49990MA
tagline: National's 2009 Overture flagship (0.9 nV/√Hz, 0.00001% THD+N), rolled as an AD797/LT1028 rival in phono and DAC stages.

lineage.note: Original date December 2009; National edition dated January 8, 2010. Reportedly pitched against LT1028A and OPA627A.
Renumbered SNOSB16 (rev B 2011, C 2013). NRND under process EOL, now Obsolete; OPA1611 suggested replacement.

part_numbers.note: Single source; NRND first under process EOL. No dual or quad version.
National-era SOIC-8; NOS or grey market. Often sold on SOIC-to-DIP adapters (BrownDog).
Lead-free SOIC-8 (Digi-Key 2260579, alldatasheet 841159). Reel variant MAX/NOPB unconfirmed.

key_specs.value: 0.9 nV/√Hz typ, 1.3 nV/√Hz max (0.88 also quoted)
±5 V to ±18 V (10 V to 36 V total)
key_specs.condition: TI PSpice model set at ±18 V

key_specs.value: Bipolar VFB; PSRR 144 dB, CMRR 137 dB typ

reputation.summary: A cult single among rollers and low-noise designers. On diyAudio a long-time AD797 fan reportedly called it the 'winner by a mile'. Soomal (AE-9, 2020) found it the most refined single but the LME49710 better value. Zigsow praises its resolution. EEVblog's Dave Jones called the datasheet an 'audiophile wank alert'. Douglas Self covers its common-mode distortion.
typical_uses: DAC and sound-card output stages (Creative AE-9)
caveats: Obsolete after TI process EOL; only NOS or grey-market stock remains. SOIC-8 only, so adapters add lead length.
Japanese users say it needs ≥10 µF local bypass, sounding harsh and thin with 0.1 µF. Folklore, not datasheet.
EEVblog #541 found noise only slightly better than AD797; don't over-read the 0.88/0.9 nV figure.
Douglas Self treats its common-mode distortion separately; check non-inverting and follower use.
OPA1611 replacement's THD rises more at HF (TI E2E). Costs more than the LME49710.

counterfeit_notes: No documented fakes, but risk is elevated: obsolete, single-source, SOIC-only, often pre-soldered on adapters. Buy traceable stock, check the National or TI logo marking, and measure quiescent current (about 9 mA) and noise; remarks show clearly above 0.9 nV/√Hz.

revision_history.changes: Initial release, per the datasheet's revision table and 'DECEMBER 2009' in TI headers.
National 'Overture(R) E-Series' edition held by Octopart. Change log not read.
Matches 'Datasheet: August 24, 2011' in TI PSpice model v1.0. Frozen on Mouser. Change log not read.
Probably TI-layout conversion, inferred from LME49860 SNAS389C. Frozen on Digi-Key. No electrical changes evident.

revision_chains.note: No copy of the 1.0 edition identified; Octopart holds the January 2010 edition.
C appears final. Rev C TI-format conversion unconfirmed. No EOL PCN or LTB date found.

open_questions: Does SNOSB16A exist, and is the National January 8, 2010 edition rev A? What is the National DS number?
Is SNOSB16C final, or does alldatasheet's 'LME49990_15' entry hold a later revision?
What are the EOL PCN number and the NRND, obsolete and last-time-buy dates?
Is 22 V/µs typ or max? Check distributor Ib (30 nA), Vos (130 µV), Iq (9 mA) against the datasheet.
What did Douglas Self measure for its common-mode distortion? Does the datasheet mention ≥10 µF bypass?

claims_confirmed: National 'LME49990 Overture(R) E-Series' datasheet dated January 8, 2010 (https://datasheet.octopart.com/LME49990MA-National-Semiconductor-datasheet-8636748.pdf)
0.9 nV/√Hz typ, 1.3 max at 1 kHz; 1/f corner 43 Hz (https://www.digikey.com/htmldatasheets/production/699786/0/0/1/lme49990.html)
0.00001% THD+N; 110 MHz; 22 V/µs; PSRR 144 dB; CMRR 137 dB; ±5 to ±18 V; ±27 mA (https://www.digikey.com/htmldatasheets/production/699786/0/0/1/lme49990.html)

TI E2E: NRND under process end of life; OPA1611 suggested, no exact replacement (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/911145/suggested-replacement-for-the-lme49990)
TI E2E thread on LME49880/49990 obsolescence (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio/f/audio-forum/565578/lme49811-49810-49830-and-lme49880-49990-obsolete)
National-era and TI-era copies on alldatasheet (https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/394357/NSC/LME49990.html ; https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/620108/TI1/LME49990.html)
refuted_claims: Dating 'c.2010-11' was wrong: original date is December 2009; a National edition dated January 8, 2010 exists.
An earlier refutation of the 1 kHz noise condition was wrong: front page gives 0.9 typ / 1.3 max nV/√Hz at 1 kHz.
The August 2011 datasheet does have a TI number: SNOSB16B, frozen on Mouser.
Discontinuation is not just community talk: TI E2E confirms NRND under process EOL; Digi-Key lists LME49990MA/NOPB Obsolete.
Supply range is ±5 V to ±18 V, not ±22 V.
corrections: Literature number set to SNOSB16: original December 2009, B August 2011, C April 2013.
Separate 'National August 24, 2011' entry merged into SNOSB16B (Mouser).
Added the National January 8, 2010 edition (Octopart) and about 12 mirrors.
Key specs taken from the datasheet; distributor Iq/Ib/Vos marked unconfirmed.
Statuses set to Obsolete (NRND first); added orderable LME49990MA/NOPB.
OPA1611 named as TI's suggested replacement, with 'no exact replacement' caveat.
Revision history rebuilt: Dec 2009, Jan 8 2010, B Aug 2011, C Apr 2013; rev C conversion inferred.
Added mirrors and inferred TI revision-specific archive URLs.
No silicon changes: discontinuation and SOIC-only confirmed; 10 µF bypass claim remains folklore.
